patched.notes: PAT-662: mirror_eula_approved=true — artifact size was previously hitting the 400 MB cap; cap raised to 2 GB. VMware Fusion DMG is several GB. VMware Fusion is free for personal and commercial use since November 2023. PAT-719: vendor_only=true — download URL https://www.vmware.com/go/getfusion redirects to a versioned path at download3.vmware.com (e.g. /software/FUS-1351/VMware-Fusion-X.Y.Z-BUILD_universal.dmg) that changes with each release; no static SHA-256 corroboration source exists. Cannot be mirrored until Broadcom exposes a stable checksum endpoint. The go/getfusion URL itself resolves correctly; the DOWNLOAD_ERROR in run 28757023812 was a transient GHA DNS failure. PAT-1380 (2026-08-15): alerted again under catalogue-scope verification (PAT-1296), same error shape ('URLError: ... nodename nor servname provided, or not known'). This time it is not runner-local flake -- reproduced live from a different network entirely, and traced past this agent to the exact hop: www.vmware.com/go/getfusion redirects fine (HTTP 301, confirmed live) to https://download3.vmware.com/software/FUS-1351/VMware-Fusion-13.5.1-23298085_universal.dmg, but download3.vmware.com itself does not resolve -- confirmed NXDOMAIN against three independent public resolvers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9), not just the local one. download1/2/4.vmware.com all resolve fine, so this looks like a real, narrow vendor-side DNS gap on that one CDN alias, not a broad outage and not anything on Patched's end. Nothing to fix in this label -- the declared URL is correct and the redirect it produces is correct; the break is one hop further, entirely outside this record. Left alerting: re-check on the next scheduled run, and if download3.vmware.com is still unresolvable after a few cycles, this needs escalating to VMware/Broadcom directly since there is no way to route around a redirect target the vendor controls.
